description:
The map illustrates the divergence of Natura 2000 (N2K) site boundaries over time, contrasting an original site definition (left panel) with an updated definition (right panel) for several sites in France, all encompassed by a stable Area of Interest (Aol).

The map displays two side-by-side views for the same set of N2K sites, labelled with identifiers such as FR7200682, FR7200683, FR7200684, FR7200685, and FR7200686.
The light orange shading represents the N2K Area of Interest (Aol), which is a buffered zone (e.g., 2 km buffer) derived from an earlier Natura 2000 site selection and remains stable across updates.
The left panel shows original Natura 2000 site boundaries, highlighted in light blue (teal), likely corresponding to an earlier database version such as Natura 2000 v2013. Internal grey lines indicate river networks or water bodies within these sites.
The right panel shows updated Natura 2000 site boundaries, highlighted in light purple (lavender), corresponding to a later database version (e.g., end2015, used for the 2018 reference year update). These updated boundaries also contain internal grey lines for water features.

The map clearly demonstrates how the shape and extent of the core N2K site boundaries (blue vs. purple) can change between different database versions while the surrounding N2K Aol (orange) remains fixed. This results in instances where the updated site boundaries (purple) either slightly deviate from the earlier boundaries (blue) within the consistent Aol, or where the Aol no longer perfectly matches the updated site shapes, as indicated by the accompanying text explaining that changes in yearly updated N2K site definitions were not adapted for already mapped N2K sites.
